prompt: The svc package returns errors as bare strings. Make them structured and auditable. Every error response from svc.api.dispatch becomes {"status": N, "error": {"code": CODE, "message": TEXT}} with the same status numbers and message texts as today. Codes: NotFound -> E_NOT_FOUND (404), Invalid -> E_INVALID (400), a plain AppError -> E_APP (500), unknown route -> E_UNKNOWN_ROUTE (404, message `unknown route`), any unexpected exception -> E_INTERNAL (500, message `internal`, never the exception text). Each error class in svc.errors carries `code` and `status` class attributes with those values, and dispatch must read them from the raised error rather than hard-coding a chain per class. Add a new Conflict error (E_CONFLICT, 409) and make rename_user raise it when another user already has the requested name (renaming a user to its own current name is fine). svc.audit.record now takes (route, status, code) and stores that 3-tuple in LOG; dispatch must record every call, code being None on success, and the route recorded for an unknown route is the requested name.
setup: python3 -c "import base64,json,os;d=json.loads(base64.b64decode(''));[(os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p) or '.',exist_ok=True),(open(p,'w').write(c) if not os.path.exists(p) else None),(os.chmod(p,0o755) if p.endswith('.sh') else None)) for p,c in d.items()]"
